interventions.body: Postoperative prognosis depends on the preoperative PSA and the prostatectomy findings. Extraprostatic extension is reported absent. Positive surgical margins is documented. Seminal vesicle invasion is reported absent. Lymphovascular invasion is documented. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are needed to refine this prognosis; a future recurrence date cannot be established from surgical risk factors alone. The fixed estimated horizon is 46.71 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 37.37–56.05 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text:
The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. The surgical findings indicate a Gleason 4+4 (ISUP grade group 3) and positive surgical margins, which are concerning features. Counterbalancing these are the absence of lymph node metastasis and the seminal vesicles not being invaded. Preoperative PSA was elevated at 8.6. The biopsy-to-prostatectomy difference is noted as the Gleason pattern and ISUP report are missing from the biopsy documentation. Nodal status is documented as no lymph node metastasis, which is a favorable finding.

The primary uncertainty lies in the postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory, as this information is currently absent. Missing nodal sampling, although the record states nodes were sampled, widens the uncertainty regarding complete nodal status. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and its trend is crucial for revising the prognosis.

attempts.text:
The patient underwent a robot-assisted radical prostatectomy with a pathological stage of pT2, Gleason 4+4 (ISUP grade group 3), and positive surgical margins. The seminal vesicles were not invaded, but lymphovascular invasion was present, and there was no lymph node metastasis documented. Preoperative PSA was 8.6.

Two primary factors drive the prognosis: the positive surgical margins and the presence of lymphovascular invasion. Countervailing findings include the absence of lymph node metastasis. The biopsy-to-prostatectomy difference is noted as the Gleason pattern and ISUP report are missing. Missing nodal sampling, although the record states nodes were sampled, widens uncertainty regarding complete nodal status.

The prognostic horizon suggests a follow-up period of approximately 46.7 months without an event. Information that would revise this prognosis significantly includes the postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory. The current data indicates a high-risk profile based on the surgical findings.

nodal_contradiction: Missing nodal sampling, although the record states nodes were sampled, widens uncertainty regarding complete nodal status
